records.title: mcp-logic
records.text:
Does: First-order logic prover and model finder (Prover9/Mace4): prove a conclusion from premises, find counterexamples, check satisfiability and consistency, abductive explanation.
Good for: Checking whether a conclusion strictly follows from stated premises; necessary vs sufficient conditions; finding a counterexample to a general rule.
Not for: Empirical questions about the world; arithmetic word problems; anything without explicit premises.

records.title: efh-core
records.text:
Does: Claim ledger with a verification gate: assert and commit claims, verify implications with Z3 plus a fidelity judge, consistency monitoring across agents, audit trail.
Good for: Turning claims into recorded knowledge only after formal verification; keeping many agents' claims consistent over time.
Not for: One-off questions; informal notes.

records.title: graph-of-thought
records.text:
Does: Runs a graph of LLM operations on its own model: generate many candidate solutions, score them, keep the best, merge and improve.
Good for: Exploring many alternative designs, drafts or solutions and pruning to the best; merging several drafts.
Not for: Single factual answers; counting or exact computation; long graphs from Cowork (60 s limit).

records.title: jev
records.text:
Does: Fast, cheap typed-judgment model: yes/no probabilities, label choice, graded scores over JSON; saved capabilities with composite scores and routing (claim_router, evidence_stance, source_relevance).
Good for: Classifying, filtering or ranking many items at once; routing; checking whether wording is supported by stated evidence; relevance of search results.
Not for: Counting, arithmetic, dates; generating text; adversarial or untrusted input as a safety gate.

records.title: wisdom-engine
records.text:
Does: Generates competing hypotheses for an observation from mechanism, narrative and constraint perspectives, eliminates them by constraints, ad hoc defences and explaining-away, then synthesizes the surviving explanation.
Good for: Diagnosing why something happened; drafting rival explanations for a symptom or bug; stress-testing a favoured explanation.
Not for: Tasks with a known answer or a fixed procedure. Its hypotheses often reword one cause, so it is a first draft of rivals, not a complete list. From Cowork only generate_hypotheses fits the 60 s limit; apply_via_negativa times out.

records.title: advanced-reasoning
records.text:
Does: Structured reasoning journal: thoughts with hypotheses, evidence, confidence and revisions, stored in a memory graph that persists across sessions.
Good for: Long investigations spanning sessions that need a persistent, revisable reasoning trail.
Not for: Short tasks; tasks whose answer does not depend on a reasoning record.

records.title: context-compressor
records.text:
Does: Compresses long text or files into summaries that keep named entities and key facts; stores searchable chunks that can be expanded later.
Good for: Fitting long documents, logs or conversation history into limited context; searching compressed notes.
Not for: Exact quotation; short texts.

records.title: PageIndex
records.text:
Does: Document library for long PDFs and reports: upload, structure-aware browsing, relevance search, and page-level retrieval.
Good for: Answering questions about long PDFs, specs, papers or reports; finding which pages discuss a topic.
Not for: Code; short documents already in context.

records.title: pdf-viewer
records.text:
Does: Displays a PDF to the user in the app and navigates or interacts with its pages.
Good for: Showing Ty a PDF or a specific page while discussing it.
Not for: Extracting or searching content in bulk.

records.title: ast-asg
records.text:
Does: Parses code into syntax trees and semantic graphs, analyzes whole projects, syncs code structure to Neo4j, structural search and pattern-based transforms.
Good for: Understanding the structure of an unfamiliar codebase; finding or refactoring all uses of a function or pattern structurally.
Not for: Prose; single small edits.

records.title: project-synapse
records.text:
Does: Knowledge graph and wiki: ingest text, formal semantic parsing, explore connections between entities, remember and recall memories over time, maintain wiki pages.
Good for: Building or querying a personal knowledge base; finding non-obvious connections between concepts in notes.
Not for: One-off lookups; code.

records.title: aseke-compass
records.text:
Does: Scaffolds analysis of human behavior, situations or conflicts using affective neuroscience (primary emotional systems) and behavioural patterns.
Good for: Understanding motivations behind a person's or group's behaviour or a conflict.
Not for: Technical or factual tasks.

records.title: advanced-writer
records.text:
Does: Fiction and narrative toolkit: brainstorm ideas, develop characters, build a world bible, choose a story structure, draft, expand and revise stories.
Good for: Writing or revising stories, novels and other narrative fiction.
Not for: Technical documentation; factual reports.

records.title: LocalREPL
records.text:
Does: Persistent Python REPLs and shells running on Ty's real computer (not the sandbox VM), keeping state across calls, with a searchable command log.
Good for: Work that needs Ty's actual machine: the GPU, local services such as Ollama or Neo4j, long-running processes, state kept across many steps.
Not for: Tasks the sandbox shell already handles, such as editing files in a connected folder.

records.title: Desktop Commander
records.text:
Does: Shell, process control, file search and editing on Ty's computer; long-running processes, SSH, reading structured files.
Good for: Managing processes and services on Ty's machine, SSH, searching the filesystem beyond connected folders.
Not for: Tasks the sandbox shell already handles in connected folders.

records.title: Context7
records.text:
Does: Looks up current documentation and code examples for libraries and frameworks.
Good for: Writing code against a library API; checking current versions, options and usage.
Not for: Non-code questions.

records.title: Shadcn UI
records.text:
Does: Source code, demos, blocks and themes for shadcn/ui React components.
Good for: Building React user interfaces with standard components and themes.
Not for: Backend code; non-React interfaces.

records.title: GitHub
records.text:
Does: GitHub repositories, files, branches, issues, pull requests and releases for Ty's account (angrysky56).
Good for: Opening or reviewing pull requests, filing issues, reading remote repos, releases.
Not for: Local-only work that is not on GitHub.

records.title: Hugging Face
records.text:
Does: Search Hugging Face models, datasets, papers and Spaces; inspect repos; run jobs and sandboxes on Hugging Face.
Good for: Finding a model or dataset for a job; reading model cards; running compute on Hugging Face.
Not for: Local GPU work on Ty's machine.

records.title: Built-in browser
records.text:
Does: Claude's browser pane: open web pages, read them, fill forms, take screenshots.
Good for: Interacting with websites that need clicking, forms, or logins; reading pages that the fetch tool cannot.
Not for: Plain web search or reading simple pages.
